extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators and research administrators preparing NIH PHS 398 grant applications (e.g., PA-13-302)
extracted.subtask_description: Completing and justifying an NIH PHS 398-style research application including Specific Aims, Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach), budget (modular/direct/indirect), and required human subjects/other compliance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIFIC AIMS — central hypothesis and three specific aims describing the goals of the proposed studies (Aim 1, Aim 2, Aim 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State a clear central hypothesis and 2–4 specific aims that flow from it. Each aim should be concise and testable and tied to overall long-term goals (e.g., elucidate mechanisms of polyomavirus replication, DDR role, and genome instability). Numbering and diagrammatic reference (Fig. 1) are used to show relationships among aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH STRATEGY A. SIGNIFICANCE — explain critical gaps in knowledge, why the problem is important, and how proposed work will advance the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the biological/medical importance (e.g., disease burden, lack of treatments), identify specific knowledge gaps, and state how the proposed studies will address them and have broad impact (A1–A3 style subpoints). Provide context and prior work supporting the importance of the question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH STRATEGY B. INNOVATION — explain conceptual, methodological, and model-system novelties that make the proposal original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate what is novel (central hypothesis, unique model system, technical approaches). Provide concrete examples: novel concepts in the field, use of a pathologically relevant primary cell model, and bridging methodologies (e.g., 2-D gels, DNA fiber assays). Explain why these innovations are important to achieving the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH STRATEGY C. APPROACH — present the experimental model, rationale, preliminary data, experimental plans for each aim, and interpretation framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit model linking hypotheses and aims, detailed experimental plans (methods, expected outcomes), discussion of preliminary studies that justify feasibility (e.g., C2 Preliminary Studies), and interpretation/alternative strategies (mechanistic model, replication intermediates, DDR assays). Demonstrate rigor (controls, quantitation) and relevance of chosen assays and cell models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Studies / Preliminary Results
rubrics_metrics.description: C2) PRELIMINARY STUDIES — present prior data showing feasibility and supporting the central hypothesis (e.g., DDR activation by BKPyV, siRNA knockdowns affecting replication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative data, representative figures, and direct evidence that supports the proposed approach (e.g., biochemical markers, viral replication assays, Southern blot, icronuclei formation). Use preliminary results to justify specific experiments and to explain how they shape proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a Pathologically Relevant Model System
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify and use an appropriate model system (e.g., primary RPTE cell culture) that is pathologically relevant and preserves normal DDR/cell-cycle regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the chosen model better recapitulates in vivo biology than transformed cell lines, and how results will therefore be more relevant. Detail advantages (permissiveness to virus, intact checkpoints) and compare to alternative systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — Senior/Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: BUDGET JUSTIFICATION Senior/Key Personnel: list named senior/key personnel with calendar months, roles, responsibilities, and percent effort (e.g., Mengxi Jiang, 4.8 calendar months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific tasks for each named individual (e.g., lead experiments, data analysis, manuscript preparation, supervise staff, weekly meetings). Provide calendar-month effort and link personnel effort to project activities and specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel Justification (other staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel for the project: list non-key personnel (graduate students, research assistants, research associates) with roles, calendar months, background, and assigned aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide short bios/qualifications, specific responsibilities mapped to aims (e.g., Specific Aim 1 lead), and justification of effort (calendar months) consistent with tasks and training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Modular Budget — Required Fields per Budget Period
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Modular Budget sections for each budget period: A. Direct Costs (Funds Requested, Direct Cost less Consortium F&A, Consortium F&A, Total Direct Costs*), B. Indirect Costs (Indirect Cost Type, Rate, Base, Funds Requested), C. Total Direct and Indirect Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide modular/direct cost requests per budget period, specify consortium F&A if applicable, include indirect cost type and rate, list the cognizant agency and the indirect cost rate agreement date, and compute totals. Repeat for each budget period and provide cumulative totals for the entire project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizant Agency / Indirect Cost Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Cognizant Agency (agency name, POC and phone) and Indirect Cost Rate Agreement Date (e.g., DHHS, Steven Zuraf, 301-492-4855; Agreement Date 09/25/2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the cognizant agency contact and the date of the current indirect cost rate agreement to validate indirect cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Income — indicate whether program income is anticipated and, if yes, list anticipated amount(s) and source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If program income is anticipated during the funded periods, provide a breakdown by budget period using the specified format; if none, leave section blank or indicate 'No.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission Statement for Non-awarded Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission Statement — indicate whether the Government is permitted to disclose the title of the proposed project and contact information if the application does not result in an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must answer Yes/No; selecting Yes allows government to disclose PI/project contact to organizations that may be interested in collaborations or investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects / Clinical Trial Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Subjects — declare whether the project involves human subjects and whether it is an Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No for human subjects and for Phase III clinical trial. If human subjects are involved, include Protection of Human Subjects section and other required human-subjects documentation (consent, IRB approvals, safety monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects / Inclusion Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Research Plan sections relating to human subjects and inclusion: Protection of Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women and Minorities; Inclusion of Children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, include all required sections: risk/benefit, recruitment, consent, monitoring plans, and plans for inclusion of women/minorities/children with justification or rationale for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC) Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Embryonic Stem Cells — indicate whether the project involves hESCs and, if yes, list registration number(s) of specific cell lines or check that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hESCs are used, reference lines from the NIH registry or indicate intention to use a registry-listed line later. Provide registry identifiers when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents (renewal applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions and Patents — for renewal applications indicate whether there are inventions/patents and whether they were previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No and provide details if applicable, per renewal reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Investigator / Change of Institution Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Change of Investigator / Change of Institution — if applicable, provide name of former PD/PI or former grantee institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete these fields when a change is being requested or reported to document continuity and prior approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Required Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Plan — attach applicable sections and supporting documents: Introduction (resubmission/revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Inclusion Sections, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plans, Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide each listed document where applicable; include Letters_of_Support_Final.pdf, Research_Strategy_Final.pdf, Specific_Aims_Final.pdf, Budget_Justification_Final.pdf, and other attachments in required formats. Ensure each attachment addresses relevant instructions and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support as part of the Research Plan attachments (e.g., Letters_of_Support_Final.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide letters that document institutional commitments, collaborator contributions, core or resource access, and other assurances; ensure they are current and specific to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plan(s) — statement(s) about sharing data, model organisms, genomic data, and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for data sharing, model organism sharing, and other required resource sharing statements as applicable; place in the Research Plan attachments and follow agency-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix — optional additional material (if applicable) accompanying the Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only allowed appendix material per agency policy; label and reference appendix items in the main application where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Budget — Multi-year Budget Period Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide modular budget entries for each budget period (Budget Period: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) with start/end dates and repeated A/B/C sections for costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete each period separately with Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, and Totals. Provide consistent dates (e.g., 04/01/YYYY to 03/31/YYYY) and ensure cumulative totals are provided in the Cumulative Budget Information section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative Budget Information and Justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative Budget Information — total costs for entire project period and budget justifications (Personnel, Consortium, Additional Narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals across all periods for direct costs, consortium F&A, indirect costs, and total costs. Attach detailed justifications: Personnel Justification, Consortium Justification, and any Additional Narrative Justification documents.
